object_description: compact two-storey volume with inscribed courtyards
design_condition: The compact volume is placed in the eastern part of the plot, preserving open space and adding tree planting to the west, while southern access is separated from neighbouring residences and the courtyards remain enclosed within the building.

positive.statement: The urban setting leaves plenty of space for the existing clinic and surrounding area.
Tree planting in front of the patient rooms creates added value for the rest of the hospital area.
The pedestrian access and driveway allow a short and direct connection to the clinic area.
The separation of the areas is clear.
The orientation of the patient rooms offers a high quality of living and prevents views of adjacent living quarters.
The therapy areas are easily accessible via the central transfer area and relatively directly from the entrance.

negative.statement: The two walking yards are only illuminated from above and offer no view.
The walking yard on the ground floor has no openings despite being located on the outside facade.
Cleaning the large glass surfaces would be rather complex.
Overall, the design remains somewhat schematic.
The external appearance with the glass elements seems over-instrumented for a forensic clinic and integrates poorly into the existing buildings.
